topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and context for the lecture on the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, naming conventions, and central biochemical role of component C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream recognition pathways and their convergence on generating surface-bound convertases to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three major downstream effector processes triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in specific complement components produce distinct clinical pathologies and disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the molecular mechanisms evolved by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture closing and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
